# Constantine Blyuz — full site text

> Energy consultant, lecturer and author. Former Deputy Director of Israel’s Natural Gas Authority (2010–2020) and Israeli diplomat. This file reproduces the English edition of cblyuz.com; the same content is published in Russian at /ru/ and in Hebrew at /he/.

Last updated: 2026-10-20

---

## Home — biography, natural gas policy, consulting portfolio, contacts

Source: https://www.cblyuz.com/en/

Constantine Blyuz
Energy Consultant, Lecturer and Author, Co-founder and Chairman of an NGO. Former Senior Government Official and Diplomat.
“The present state of our energy sector is disappointing, while its future is brilliant. Yet when that future becomes the present, it is disappointing once more—and the next future is brilliant again.”
(c) Constantine Blyuz
01 Biography
One biography, several chapters
“The government always blinks first—because it has more eyes.” (c) Constantine Blyuz
Since 2000, my work has focused on the Israeli and regional energy industry. From 2010 to 2020, I served as Deputy Director of the Natural Gas Authority; for more than a decade, I have also taught at academic institutions and spoken at local and international forums.
Since 2023, I have worked as a consultant to industry and institutional clients — including power system operators, IPPs, infrastructure companies, local gas distribution companies, energy exchanges, investment institutions, rating agencies, insurance brokers and others.
Beyond energy, my experience includes two years as an Israeli diplomat, management of an artistic agency, co-founding enterprises and charitable NGOs, and presenting my first musical. My first novel was published in 2025; a second is scheduled for publication in 2026.
02 Natural Gas Policy
Main Activities as an Energy Regulator
“We wanted to do good deeds, but feared the wider implications.” (c) Constantine Blyuz
2004–2009
Early Industry Development
I was involved in developing the Israeli natural gas industry from its early stages, first as Economics & Tariffs Manager. During this period, I participated in negotiations on natural gas import contracts with Egypt and Shell, formerly BG.
View details → Selected achievements
01 Developed the methodology and model for natural gas transmission tariffs.
02 Created the conditions for financing the construction of the transmission system through negotiations with international rating agencies, including S&P and Moody’s, and financial institutions.
03 Prepared the Master Plan for the Israeli Natural Gas Market through 2035.
04 Formulated the General Transmission Agreement and Standard Distribution Agreement — commercially oriented contracts applicable to all market participants.
05 Regulated natural gas imports from Egypt.
2010–2020
Deputy Director of the Natural Gas Authority
From 2010 to 2020, I served as Deputy Director of the Natural Gas Authority and participated in many of the major decision-making processes shaping Israel’s natural gas policy.
View details → Selected achievements
01 Prepared and issued six tenders for Local Distribution Companies and CNG shippers, and awarded licenses.
02 Formulated and implemented a program to accelerate the development of distribution networks, Tochnit Haheatsa.
03 Submitted statements and affidavits in various court proceedings.
04 Established service orders and rules for license holders and handled arbitrations between license holders and consumers.
05 Represented Israel as a speaker at international forums in Ukraine, Austria, Italy, Belgium, Cyprus and elsewhere.
2009–2019
Gas Supply and Export Agreements
From 2009 to 2019, I participated in negotiations involving lease terms for the Tamar, Leviathan and Karish fields, as well as export agreements with Jordan, Egypt and the Palestinian Authority.
View details → Key milestones
2010 Tamar Lease awarded.
2014 Leviathan Lease awarded.
2016 First export agreement with Jordan finalized.
2017 Karish Lease awarded.
2018 Large export contracts with Egypt and Jordan finalized.
2019 Export agreement via the offshore Ashkelon–Al Arish pipeline prepared.
2010–2018
Long-Term Policy and LNG
I participated in the two interministerial committees established to examine Israel’s long-term natural gas policy, in 2012 and in the revised process in 2018. From 2010 to 2013, I served as coordinator of the government’s efforts to bring LNG to Israel.
View details → Selected achievements
01 Prepared the official forecasts of natural gas demand in Israel in 2007, 2012, 2014 and 2018, which were used by the Government of Israel in formulating its policies.
02 Initiated and led the Israeli LNG project, including the installation of the STL buoy and the five-year contract with Excelerate’s Hadera Gateway FSRU. The project was completed in 2013.
03 Since 2016, ship-to-ship LNG operations have been implemented in the open port, which was state-of-the-art at the time.
03 Cases
As an energy consultant
Regulators, state-owned companies, gas distributors, fuel and energy companies — in Israel and the region.
Business development, economic and regulatory consulting — tariffs, agreements, annual budget and financial supervision
Consulting on entering the electricity market as a virtual power supplier; defining strategies of power procurement and marketing in the residential sector
Consulting on entering new markets in Eastern Europe; developing market-entry strategies and revenue-extraction & monetization models
Supporting negotiations with a dozen Israeli energy companies
Participating in the international team providing consulting services to the Israeli Ministry of Energy — long-term policy planning for the Israeli energy sector
Consulting on the implications of a pricing reform proposed by the electricity market regulator
Preparing an opinion on regulated tariff policy changes; introducing a new pricing model based on unification and standardization of cash flows from multiple charges
Consulting the team responsible for promoting the long-term project to build a gas-fired power plant in Hebron; defining the terms of gas purchase and connection agreements
Assisting in a long-term project to establish a regional energy exchange; taking part in negotiations with Hungarian and German partners
Preparing an opinion on the consequences of the rates and standard distribution agreement reform proposed by the gas industry regulator
Preparing an opinion on the long-term gas transmission fee and its components; forecasting future natural gas transmission charges
Teaching a semester course on “Oil, Gas, and Geopolitics” (since 2015), covering decisions taken by governments and industry leaders over the past decade and a half
Consulting regarding the participation in several energy tenders
Consulting regarding deep connections of potential consumers to the natural gas distribution network
Teaching a semester course “Oil products conversion”

Articles and interviews

## The musical: No One in Front of the Mirror

Source: https://www.cblyuz.com/en/musical.html

← Back
Musical
No One in Front of the Mirror
Musical Book & lyrics Full synopsis
The musical consists of three independent movements with two characters each – female and male. Three of them are historic figures; others are fictional, the last two are even nameless. Three of the characters enter the most dramatic circumstances in their lives; the drama of the others is overshoot and, in some way, ironic.
The libretto was interpreted into a musical together with the Ukrainian composer Andrey Ehrlichman; the world premiere was presented on July 28th, 2024, in Odessa.
1. King Henry VI and Margaret d’Anjou
Scotland, 1470. Henry VI, mentally unstable king of England (who was also crowned as a king of France in 1431), lives in a small farmhouse, hidden by his followers. His wife, Queen Margaret, the most dominant figure of the War of Roses, comes to convince Henry coming back to the English throne. Although he is quite happy in his simple asylum, and even tries to convince her to abandon the struggle (aria “come to my kingdom of denial”), she is much more assertive and eventually he agrees to join her. In their final duet she sings about future victories and glory while he is singing on devastation and death.
2. Cleopatra
Alexandria, around 50 B. C. The young princess is trying to get rid of her anxiety and boredom by proclaiming an edict: she is ready to spend a night with anyone who is ready to be executed the next morning. The young locksmith Yanir, who is in love with her, accepts the challenge, and, unlike previous applicants, does not change his intentions and causes Cleopatra’s to fall in love. Alas, he will die in the morning, and she cannot change her order. She sings the aria “The morning is coming, it’s closer and closer and only an hour left”, and he is committing suicide. She puts his head in her collection of the beheaded; finally, she cancels her edict and peacefully falls asleep.
3. Dismissal
Nowadays. Anywhere. Two company employees, He and She, get information that one of them will be fired. They are moving from frustration to anger (for many years they have been both loyal and efficient), while in parallel receiving various hints from the administration. He takes things more philosophically (“And to be interrupted in order to be understood”), she prefers to fight and convinces him that both must resign; however, in the end only one resignation letter is going to be submitted.
